title: Do jellyfish sleep, even without a brain?
blurb: Upside-down jellyfish have no brain, only a net of nerves. Students at Caltech showed they still have a sleep-like rest at night, and feel tired after a disturbed night.

original.title: The Jellyfish Cassiopea Exhibits a Sleep-like State
original.authors: Nath, R. D., Bedbrook, C. N., Abrams, M. J., and others

cards.b: People sleep. So do dogs, birds, fish and even worms and flies. All of them have a brain, a control centre for the body. Jellyfish have no brain. They have only a loose net of nerves spread through the body. Can an animal without a brain still sleep?

Ravi Nath, Claire Bedbrook and Michael Abrams led this study at Caltech, the California Institute of Technology, in the United States. They worked with senior scientists Lea Goentoro, Viviana Gradinaru, Paul Sternberg, David Prober and others. They published in 2017.

Upside-down jellyfish lie on the sand and pulse, squeezing and relaxing their bell about once a second. The team filmed 23 jellyfish for six days and nights and counted every pulse. They also lifted each jellyfish in a mesh tube and let them go in open water. Then they watched how fast each one started pulsing and swam back down.

img.alt: An upside-down jellyfish resting on stones in shallow water, with the round bell pressed against the bottom.
img.credit: Yoannis Domínguez, CC BY 4.0, via iNaturalist

cards.b: At night the jellyfish pulsed about one third less, and often paused. When dropped at night, they took longer to start pulsing and to reach the bottom, like a sleepy person. When the team kept them awake at night with puffs of water, they pulsed less the next day. They were catching up on lost rest.

img.alt: An upside-down jellyfish floating in open water, with a spotted bell and frilly arms hanging below.
img.credit: Robin White, CC BY 4.0, via iNaturalist

cards.b: The jellyfish showed all three signs that scientists use for sleep: they rest, they are slower to react, and they catch up after missing rest. Melatonin, a body chemical that makes people sleepy, also made them rest more. This was one kind of jellyfish in a lab. Scientists call it a sleep-like state, to be careful.

Jellyfish belong to a very old group of animals. If they sleep without a brain, sleep probably began very early in the story of animals, before brains existed. So sleep must do something deeply important for every animal. Scientists still do not know exactly what that job is.

Be a sleep scientist for a week. Each morning, write down what time you went to sleep and what time you woke. Also test how quick you are. Ask someone to give you the same quick sum at breakfast, such as 7 times 8, and note how long you take. After a late night, are you slower? Like the jellyfish, do you catch up with a longer sleep the next night?

A jellyfish has no brain but still rests in a sleep-like way. So is sleep something the brain does, or something the whole body needs? Some scientists think sleep helps us remember. Others think sleep repairs the body. What do you think sleep is for?

words.m: a rest that has the signs of sleep, used when scientists want to be careful
nerves spread through the body like a net, with no brain in charge
the squeeze and relax of a jellyfish's bell, like a heartbeat you can see
a chemical the body makes at night that helps people feel sleepy
